structural_memory.memory: Shipboard hydraulic-power service spans owner/manager, master, engineering and relevant deck crews, shore technical support, hydraulic pump/accumulator/actuator equipment or service actors and port or yard support. Operating observation, equipment service and shore intervention should remain distinct roles rather than one vendor directory.

Hydraulic pump or source readiness is distinct from electrical prime-power availability and from delivered hydraulic service. A motor or engine drive can be available while a hydraulic source is restricted, and a hydraulic constraint does not by itself prove an electrical, mechanical or control root cause.

Reservoir inventory or capacity confidence is distinct from fluid-condition confidence. Sufficient apparent inventory does not establish acceptable fluid condition or delivered service, while uncertain condition does not by itself prove inadequate inventory.

Accumulator or other stored-energy confidence is a separate service dimension from active pump readiness. Stored-energy availability may temporarily support or buffer a consumer while a source state is changing, but exact charge, pressure, capacity and operating logic are deferred.

Hydraulic distribution or path availability is separate from source readiness. A source can be available while a distribution segment, interface or consumer branch is restricted; exact piping, valves, manifolds, pressures and lineups are not retained.

Consumer scope should remain explicit. Steering-related equipment, deck machinery and other hydraulic consumers may share a source or distribution layer but can have independent availability states; one consumer outage does not establish loss of the whole hydraulic service.

Hydraulic demand and available service margin are distinct from simple pump-running state. A source may be running yet margin can be constrained by simultaneous consumers, restriction, stored-energy state or distribution scope; exact loads, pressures and rates remain deferred.

Fluid-condition or assurance confidence should remain distinct from physical reservoir inventory and pump availability. Missing, delayed or uncertain condition evidence can make service acceptability uncertain without proving a pump or actuator failure, while a service symptom does not establish contamination or fluid degradation.

Hydraulic-service degradation follows a defensive lifecycle: observation, uncertain source/reservoir/accumulator/distribution/consumer scope, affected-state identification, restriction or unavailability, bounded isolation, restoration indication and post-restoration verification. No hydraulic operating or troubleshooting procedure is retained.

Restriction or isolation should preserve affected scope such as source/pump, reservoir or condition-assurance function, accumulator/stored-energy function, distribution branch or consumer interface. One scope may be unavailable while other hydraulic service remains usable; exact valve positions, actuator controls and sequences remain deferred.

Hydraulic power can depend on electrical or mechanical drive, controls/monitoring, cooling and supporting fluid-management equipment, but dependency observations are not root-cause proof. A support loss can degrade hydraulic service, while a hydraulic constraint does not establish which upstream dependency failed.

Hydraulic degradation can propagate into selected steering, deck-machinery or other consumer availability, but those downstream effects are not by themselves proof of a pump, reservoir, accumulator, distribution, fluid-condition or actuator root cause.

Restoration can have multiple timestamps: source readiness returns, reservoir/condition confidence is re-established, accumulator confidence returns, distribution scope is restored and each affected consumer is separately re-verified. A restarted pump or cleared indication does not prove full hydraulic-service recovery.

P070 electrical power and P082 hydraulic power are separate utility layers. Electrical availability can support a hydraulic source without proving reservoir, accumulator, distribution or consumer readiness; a hydraulic constraint does not establish an electrical fault.

P078 compressed air and P082 hydraulic power share generated/stored/distributed utility vocabulary but remain independent media and service chains. Receiver reserve does not prove hydraulic accumulator confidence, and hydraulic availability does not prove pneumatic service.

P080 lubricating-oil service and P082 hydraulic service both involve oil-like fluids, pumps and condition confidence, but lubrication delivery and hydraulic power transmission are independent functions; lubricant inventory/condition does not prove hydraulic service and vice versa.

P067 generic equipment lifecycle remains distinct from delivered hydraulic service. Pump, accumulator, actuator or control equipment condition can inform component state without proving reservoir margin, distribution availability or consumer-service outcome.
Equipment readiness, maintenance, shore support and component lifecycle mechanics overlap the generic marine-equipment lifecycle recovered in P067.
Scoped degradation, dependency, restriction/isolation and verified-restoration mechanics overlap prior shipboard utility-service passes; P082 applies them specifically to hydraulic power.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: Exact hydraulic topology, reservoir capacities/levels, fluid grades/specifications, pressures, flow rates, accumulator charge, piping/manifolds/valves, actuator controls, instrumentation and current configuration are intentionally not retained.

Exact hydraulic source selection, charging, alignment, distribution, consumer operation, isolation, depressurization, troubleshooting, flushing, maintenance or emergency procedures are outside this blind pass.
Named hydraulic equipment/service providers, vessel failures/incidents/deficiencies, inspection findings and current readiness require claim-scoped Evidence.
Private/regional marine hydraulic equipment/service lineages plus historical non-English predecessor terminology remain deferred for source archaeology.

epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive hydraulic-power service orientation/source-discovery output. It is not steering, deck-machinery, hydraulic maintenance, safety or vessel-operating advice and does not establish any exact topology, capacity, level, fluid specification, pressure, flow rate, accumulator charge, piping/valve lineup, actuator control, instrumentation, procedure, provider, incident, deficiency, inspection finding or current-readiness fact.
stop_reason: The hydraulic-power service chain is recalled at useful structural resolution: source readiness, reservoir inventory/condition confidence, accumulator/stored-energy confidence, distribution availability, consumer scope, demand/margin, dependencies, scoped restriction/isolation and verified restoration are separable states. Further detail would become vessel-, pump-, reservoir-, accumulator-, pressure-, fluid-, piping-, actuator-, procedure-, provider- or incident-specific and is deferred to claim-scoped Evidence.
